chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about the child, when can he fast? He said: When he is strong upon fasting.
ai.seo_question: When should a child start fasting according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Sama'ah reports asking Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the fasting of children, who replied that they should fast once they possess the physical strength (*quwwa*) to endure it. This establishes the principle of *Tadrib* (training) rather than obligation (*Wujub*), allowing parents to gradually accustom children to the discipline of fasting before puberty, a practice deeply rooted in Shia fiqh as a preparatory step for the full burden of Sharia.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,
‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the child, when can he Fast?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he is strong upon the Fasting’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah, who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a child when he is required to fast.
He (the Imam) said, ‘When he is able to fast he must fast.’”
